seeds.goal: You can write an email with your news: react to what your friend wrote, give two or three pieces of your own news with details, and ask questions back.
seeds.why: This is the email everybody writes and almost nobody answers well: the news arrives without dates, without details and without a single question in return.
seeds.ex: Aigerim answered a pen-friend point by point and asked two questions. The reply came the same evening — the first time in four months.
seeds.read: Read the email and find one thing: what has changed in Aigerim's week since September?
seeds.task: Write an email with your news (80–110 words): thank your friend for their letter, react to one thing they wrote, give two pieces of your own news with details, ask two questions and close warmly.
model: Thank them and react to their news
Thanks for your last email. I am really glad the new school is going well — the photo of your classroom is enormous!
Give your first news with a detail
As for me, I have started working at a bookshop on Saturdays, from ten until four.
It is not much money, but I have already read six books that I would never have bought.
My family has also moved to a flat near the park, so I walk to school in twelve minutes instead of taking two buses.
What are your plans for the summer? Are you still going to Spain with your cousins?
Write soon and send photos. Aigerim.
phr: It was great to hear from you.
Было здорово получить от тебя весточку.
As for me, I have started …

I have started working at a bookshop on Saturdays.
I work there from ten until four.
I have already read six books this month.
My family has moved to a flat near the park.
I walk to school in twelve minutes instead of taking two buses.
What are your plans for the summer?
I did not expect to like the job.
The flat we found is smaller but much warmer.

Why the news matters to me

seeds.sub: What has changed since you last wrote

seeds.goal: You can review an app or a service: say what it does, what works, what does not, who it suits and whether it is worth the space on a phone.
seeds.why: Reviews are the writing people actually read before spending money. One honest weakness makes the whole review believable.
seeds.ex: Damir's review of a vocabulary app named the one thing it does badly. It became the top comment in the school chat.
seeds.read: Read the review and find one thing: what does the writer say the app does badly?
seeds.task: Write a review of an app you use (80–110 words): what it is for, how long you have used it, one thing it does well with an example, one weakness, who it suits and your verdict.
model: Name the app and what it does
Anki is a free app for learning vocabulary with cards.
Say how long you have used it
I have used it every day since January, mostly on the bus.
Say what works, with an example
The best thing is that it shows a word again exactly when you are about to forget it: I still remember words I learned in February and never revised on purpose.
Ten minutes a day is enough for about thirty new words a week.
However, the app looks like a program from 2005, and setting it up for the first time took me almost an hour.
It suits people who are ready to spend one boring evening at the start and then forget about the settings.
For vocabulary it is the only app I have not deleted after a month.

Десяти минут в день хватает на …
It is the only app I have not deleted.
Это единственное приложение, которое я не удалил.
sent: Anki is a free app for learning vocabulary.
I have used it every day since January.
It shows a word again before you forget it.
I still remember words I learned in February.
Ten minutes a day is enough for thirty words a week.
However, the app looks very old.
Setting it up took me almost an hour.
It suits people who like simple tools.
I have not deleted it after a month.
This app is more useful than any game.

There is one thing that will put people off.

seeds.title: A review of an app
seeds.sub: Would you tell a friend to install it?

seeds.goal: You can complain in an email: say what you bought and when, what went wrong, what you have already done and what you want the shop to do.
seeds.why: At this level a complaint stops being a description of your feelings and becomes a request with facts behind it.
seeds.ex: Nurgul's eight-line email got a replacement in four days, because the last sentence said exactly what she wanted.
seeds.read: Read the email and find one thing: what exactly does the writer ask the shop to do?
seeds.task: Write a complaint email (90–120 words): what you ordered and when, what is wrong with it, what you have already tried, what you want and by when.
model: Say what you ordered and when
On 14 April I ordered a pair of running shoes from your website, order number 20514.
The shoes arrived on 22 April, but they are size 41 and I ordered size 39.
In addition, the box was open and one shoe has a mark on the side.
Say what you have already done
I have already sent two messages through the website form, but nobody has answered.
I would like to exchange them for size 39, or to get my money back if that size is not available.
Could you reply before 5 May? Yours faithfully, Nurgul Amanova.
phr: I am writing about order number …
I would like to exchange it for …
Я хотел бы обменять это на …
… or to get my money back.
Не могли бы вы ответить до …?
sent: On 14 April I ordered a pair of running shoes.
The shoes arrived eight days later.
They are size 41 and I ordered size 39.
The box was open when it arrived.
One shoe has a mark on the side.
I have already sent two messages.
I would like to exchange them for a smaller size.
This is the second order with a problem.
topics: Size 41 instead of 39, an open box and a mark on one shoe.
There are three things wrong with this order.

I have already tried the normal way.
An exchange for size 39, or my money back if you do not have it.

seeds.title: A short complaint email
seeds.sub: Say what is wrong and what you want

seeds.goal: You can write instructions: say what the reader will do, list what they need, give the steps in order and add one warning.
seeds.why: Instructions are the only genre with an instant test: either the reader can do it or your text failed.
seeds.ex: Aisultan wrote the instructions for the school printer. The queue of people asking for help disappeared in a week.
seeds.read: Read the instructions and find one thing: what should you do if the printer shows a red light?
seeds.task: Write instructions for something practical (80–110 words): what the reader will achieve, what they need, four steps in order, one warning and what to do if it goes wrong.
model: Say what the reader will do
Here is how to print from your phone on the library printer.
You need the school wifi, the app Smart Print and your student number.
First, open the app and choose 'Library-2', not 'Library-1' — the first printer is for teachers.
Then choose your file and set 'black and white', because colour printing costs ten times more.
After that, type your student number and press Send. Nothing happens at the printer yet.
Finally, go to the printer, type the same number on the small screen and press the green button.
Say what to do if it fails
If the screen shows a red light, the paper has finished: ask at the desk instead of opening the machine.
sent: Here is how to print from your phone.
You need the school wifi and the app.
First, open the app and choose Library-2.
The first printer is only for teachers.
Colour printing costs ten times more.
Type your student number and press Send.
Nothing happens at the printer yet.
If the screen shows a red light, the paper has finished.
Do not open the machine yourself.
Ask at the desk instead of opening it.
topics: The school wifi, the app and your student number — nothing else.
Everything you need before you start.
Open, choose the printer, choose the file, send, type the number.
The whole process is five actions.
A red light means the paper has finished, not that the machine is broken.
One signal is worth knowing in advance.

seeds.sub: So that a stranger can follow them

seeds.goal: You can tell a story about something that went wrong: set the scene, tell the events in order, describe the moment it went wrong and finish with what changed.
seeds.why: A story about a mistake is easier to write than a story about a success, and it teaches you the past continuous and the past simple in the same paragraph.
seeds.ex: Zarina wrote about missing a train. Her teacher used the last two lines to show the class how to end a story.
seeds.read: Read the story and find one thing: why did the writer miss the train?
seeds.task: Write a story about a mistake you made (90–120 words): set the scene, tell what happened in order, describe the moment you realised, say what you did, and finish with what you do differently now.
model: Last September I was travelling alone for the first time, from Almaty to Shymkent.
I arrived at the station forty minutes early and sat down with a coffee and my headphones.
The train was on platform three, and I was so sure about it that I never looked at the board again.
At 14:05 a woman asked me why I was still sitting there. My train had left from platform five at 14:00.
For about ten seconds I could not think at all.
I ran to the ticket office, explained the situation and bought a seat on the evening train, which cost me almost everything I had.
Now I check the board every ten minutes, even when I am completely sure.
phr: At … a woman asked me why …
Сағат … бір әйел неге … деп сұрады.
For about ten seconds I could not …
sent: Last September I was travelling alone for the first time.
I arrived at the station forty minutes early.
I sat down with a coffee and my headphones.
I never looked at the board again.
My train had left from platform five.
For ten seconds I could not think.
I ran to the ticket office and explained the situation.
The evening ticket cost me almost everything.
Now I check the board every ten minutes.
I was so sure that I stopped listening.

Everything about that morning looked fine.
A woman asked why I was still sitting there at five past two.
The moment I understood came from a stranger.

The habit I built that day has never left me.
ideas: A description of the whole station
seeds.title: A story about a mistake
seeds.sub: What happened, and what you learned

seeds.goal: You can describe a place you know well: where it is, what you notice first, what people do there, when to go and why it matters to you.
seeds.why: Weak descriptions use 'beautiful' three times. Strong ones give three details a reader can picture — and that skill carries into every level above.
seeds.ex: Alua described a bakery near her school in ninety words. Two classmates went to find it the same week.
seeds.read: Read the description and find one thing: what is the best time to go there?
seeds.task: Describe a place you know well (90–120 words): where it is, what you notice first, what people do there, the best time to go, and why it matters to you.
model: Say what the place is and where
There is a small bakery on Tulebayev Street, between a pharmacy and a car repair shop.
You notice it before you see it, because the smell of hot bread comes out through the open door.
There are only four tables, and three of them are always taken by the same men, who have been drinking tea there since it opened.
Students come after school, buy one bun and stay for an hour, and nobody ever asks them to leave.
The best time is half past three, when the second batch of bread comes out of the oven.
A bun costs 150 tenge, which is why the place is full of people who have no money.
Say why it matters to you
I wrote most of my exam notes at the fourth table, and I still go there when I need to think.
phr: There is a small … on … Street.
You notice it before you see it, because …
Замечаешь его раньше, чем видишь, потому что …
Я до сих пор хожу туда, когда …
It is my place to think.
sent: There is a small bakery on Tulebayev Street.
The smell of hot bread comes through the door.
There are only four tables inside.
The same men have been drinking tea there for years.
Students come after school and stay for an hour.
Nobody ever asks them to leave.
The best time is half past three.
A bun costs one hundred and fifty tenge.
I wrote most of my exam notes at that table.
This bakery is quieter than any library.
topics: Four tables, three of them always taken by the same men.
The size of the place explains everything about it.
Students buy one bun and stay an hour, and nobody asks them to leave.
The rules here are not written anywhere.
Half past three, when the second batch comes out of the oven.
Timing changes the whole experience.

seeds.sub: A place through three details

seeds.goal: You can state an opinion in public: agree or disagree with a specific point, give one reason, one example from your life, and admit one thing on the other side.
seeds.why: An opinion without a reason is noise. At this level the whole task is: claim, reason, example — in three sentences.
seeds.ex: Berik commented on a post about mobile phones at school. The author replied to him because his example was concrete.
seeds.read: Read the comment and find one thing: what example from his own school does the writer give?
seeds.task: Write a comment on a post about homework at the weekend (80–110 words): say what you agree or disagree with, give one reason, one example from your school, admit one point on the other side, and end with a question.
model: I do not agree that weekend homework helps students to remember more.
The reason is simple: most of us do it on Sunday evening, in one hour, without thinking about it at all.
Give an example from your life
In my class the teacher stopped setting weekend tasks in October, and our test results in November were exactly the same as before.
Admit one point on the other side
Admittedly, in exam years the situation is different, because there is simply no other time.
So my opinion is about years seven to nine, not about everybody.
Has anybody here seen results actually fall after weekend homework was cancelled?

Так что моё мнение о …, а не о …
Яғни менің пікірім … туралы, … туралы емес.

Most of us do it on Sunday evening.
The teacher stopped setting weekend tasks in October.
Our test results were exactly the same.
In exam years the situation is different.
There is simply no other time.

seeds.sub: Your view, with one reason and one example

seeds.goal: You can ask for help in writing: explain the situation briefly, say exactly what you need, say how long it will take and offer something in return.
seeds.why: A vague request gets a vague answer. Naming the exact task and its size is what turns a favour into a yes.
seeds.ex: Aida asked a teacher for twenty minutes, not for 'help with the project'. She got the twenty minutes on Thursday.
seeds.read: Read the message and find one thing: how much time does the writer ask for?
seeds.task: Write a message asking for help (80–110 words): the situation, exactly what you need, how long it takes, when you are free, what you offer in return and how they can refuse.
model: I am preparing a project about water quality for the science week in March.
I have collected the results, but I do not know how to show them in a chart that makes sense.
Could you look at my two charts and tell me which one is clearer? I do not need help with the text.
It should take about twenty minutes.
I am free after lessons on Tuesday and Thursday, or any time during the long break.
If March is too busy, I completely understand — in that case I will ask in the science club.

I do not need help with …
If … is too busy, I understand.

I have collected the results already.
I do not know how to show them clearly.

seeds.goal: You can apologise properly: say sorry, explain briefly without excuses, say what you will do to fix it and what you will change.
seeds.why: An apology that is only 'sorry' costs nothing. The part the reader remembers is what you promise to do next.
seeds.ex: Alisher apologised for missing a group meeting and listed what he would finish by Friday. The group kept him in the project.
seeds.read: Read the message and find one thing: what will the writer do before Friday?
seeds.task: Write an apology (80–110 words): say sorry, explain briefly, admit the effect on the others, say exactly what you will do to fix it, what you will change and close.
model: I am really sorry that I missed our group meeting on Tuesday.
My little brother was ill and I had to stay with him until my mother came home at eight.
Do not hide behind the reason
That explains why I was not there, but not why I did not write: I could have sent one message at four o'clock and I did not.
I know that four people waited half an hour and that the plan for the presentation is still not finished.
I have already written the introduction and the part about the survey, and I will send both to the group chat before Friday.
From now on I will write in the chat as soon as I know I am late, even if it is only ten minutes.
phr: That explains why … , but not why …
Это объясняет, почему …, но не почему …
I could have … and I did not.
sent: I am really sorry that I missed the meeting.
My little brother was ill on Tuesday.
I had to stay with him until eight o'clock.
I could have sent one message at four.
Four people waited half an hour for me.
The plan for the presentation is still not finished.
I have already written the introduction.
I will send both parts before Friday.
From now on I will write as soon as I know.

seeds.sub: Sorry, why, and what happens now

seeds.goal: You can compare two options: choose two or three points of comparison, apply each to both, and recommend one for a specific person.
seeds.why: Comparison is where comparatives finally have a job. The trick is to compare on the same points, not to describe A and then describe B.
seeds.ex: Kamila compared two phones for her aunt and named the criteria first. Her aunt bought the one she recommended.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: who does the writer recommend the cheaper phone to?
seeds.task: Compare two things you know well (90–120 words): name the two options, compare them on three points, say where the difference is biggest, and recommend one for a specific kind of person.
model: Name the two options and the points
I compared two phones for my aunt: a new mid-range model and a two-year-old flagship, on price, battery and camera.
The older flagship is 30 per cent cheaper, and the difference is bigger than it looks, because the price of the new one does not include a case or a charger.
The battery is where the new phone wins clearly: it lasts a day and a half, while the older one needs charging by six in the evening.
The cameras are almost the same in daylight, but the older flagship is still better at night, which surprised me.
Say where the difference matters most
The biggest practical difference is not the camera but the battery, because a phone that dies at six is useless for somebody who works late.
For my aunt, who takes photographs of her garden and charges her phone at home, the older model is the better buy.
Say who should choose the other one
For somebody who is out all day, the new one is worth the extra money.
phr: I compared two … on price, … and …
Я сравнил два … по цене, … и …
Мен екі … бағасы, … және … бойынша салыстырдым.
For somebody who … , … is the better buy.

The older flagship is thirty per cent cheaper.

The cameras are almost the same in daylight.

My aunt charges her phone at home every night.
For somebody who is out all day, the new one wins.

A day and a half against needing a charger by six in the evening.

seeds.sub: Which one, and for whom

seeds.goal: You can write about an experience: set it in time and place, tell what happened, describe the moment that mattered and say what it changed.
seeds.why: This is the genre that turns 'it was interesting' into a text somebody wants to read: the difference is one concrete moment.
seeds.ex: Ruslan wrote about his first day as a volunteer. His teacher read it aloud because of one sentence about a queue.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what moment does the writer say he still remembers?
seeds.task: Write about an experience you remember (90–120 words): when and where it was, what you expected, what actually happened, the moment that stayed with you and what it changed.
model: Last winter I spent three Saturdays as a volunteer in a shelter for stray dogs outside Almaty.
I thought the hardest part would be the cold, or the smell, or the work itself.
In fact the hardest part was the queue of people at the gate on Sunday morning, who had come to leave their dogs there.
One man stood for twenty minutes with a small brown dog in his arms and did not go in. Then he turned around and took it home again.
I still do not know whether that was a happy ending or the beginning of a worse one.
I cleaned cages, carried food and learned the names of eleven dogs in three weeks.
Since then I have stopped saying that people who leave animals are simply cruel; some of them stand at the gate for twenty minutes.

Тот день изменил то, как я …

seeds.goal: You can give advice: name the problem, give two or three suggestions with reasons, warn about one thing and leave the decision to the reader.
seeds.why: Advice that starts with 'you must' is ignored. Advice that starts with 'what worked for me' is read to the end.
seeds.ex: Dana wrote advice for year sevens about starting a second language. The school printed it for the September pack.
seeds.read: Read the advice and find one thing: what does the writer say not to do?
seeds.task: Write advice for a younger student (90–120 words): name the problem they face, give three suggestions with reasons, warn about one thing, and leave the decision to them.
model: In year seven almost everybody starts a second language, and by December half of the class has decided they are 'not a languages person'.
Usually that decision comes after one bad test, not after a year of trying.
Give the first suggestion with a reason
The first thing I would do is learn ten words a week rather than fifty before a test, because fifty words on Thursday evening are gone by Monday.
Secondly, read something you would read anyway — comments under a video count — because five minutes every day beats an hour on Sunday.
You could also record yourself speaking for one minute a month and keep the files: in March you will hear the difference that you cannot feel.
The one thing I would not do is compare yourself with the two students who lived abroad — that comparison teaches you nothing.
None of this is a rule. Try one of the three for a month and keep whichever one you did not have to force yourself to do.

… because fifty words on Thursday are gone by Monday.
… потому что пятьдесят слов в четверг исчезнут к понедельнику.
… себебі бейсенбідегі елу сөз дүйсенбіде ұмытылады.
The one thing I would not do is …
None of this is a rule.

Half of the class gives up by December.
That decision comes after one bad test.
I would learn ten words a week instead of fifty.
Fifty words on Thursday are gone by Monday.
Five minutes every day beats an hour on Sunday.
You could record yourself for one minute a month.
In March you will hear the difference.
Do not compare yourself with students who lived abroad.
Keep the one you did not have to force.
topics: Ten words a week, not fifty on Thursday evening.
The first suggestion is about size, not effort.
Five minutes every day beats an hour on Sunday.
The second is about frequency.
Do not compare yourself with the two students who lived abroad.

ideas: A story about my own marks
seeds.title: Advice to a younger student
seeds.sub: What you know now and did not know then

seeds.goal: You can describe a person: their role, what they look like, what they are like, one habit and a short story that proves it.
seeds.why: Adjectives alone describe nobody. One story at the end is what makes a description true.
seeds.ex: Miras described a school caretaker for a class project. Three teachers said they recognised him from the second line.
seeds.read: Read the description and find one thing: what story shows that this person notices everything?
seeds.task: Describe a person you see often (90–120 words): who they are, what they look like, what they are like, one habit, and a short story that shows their character.
model: Sabit Agai has been the caretaker of our school for nineteen years.
He is a short man in his sixties with grey hair and hands that are always slightly dirty.
He wears the same blue jacket in October and in April, and a hat only when it is below minus fifteen.
He speaks very little, but he notices everything that happens in the building.
Every morning he walks around the whole school before the first bell, always in the same direction.
Last winter he found a first-class boy asleep in the sports hall at seven in the morning and, instead of taking him to the head teacher, gave him tea and called his grandmother.
Say what you think of them
Most of us have never had a real conversation with him, and all of us would notice immediately if he were not there.

He is a short man in his sixties with …
Это невысокий мужчина за шестьдесят с …
Ол — алпыстан асқан, … аласа бойлы адам.
He wears the same … in October and in April.
Он носит одну и ту же … и в октябре, и в апреле.
Ол қазанда да, сәуірде де сол … киеді.
All of us would notice if he were not there.
Все бы заметили, если бы его не было.

He is a short man with grey hair.
He wears the same blue jacket all autumn.
He speaks very little, but he notices everything.
Every morning he walks around the whole school.
Last winter he found a boy asleep in the hall.
He gave the boy tea and called his grandmother.
He did not take him to the head teacher.
Most of us have never really talked to him.
We would notice at once if he were not there.

The facts about him barely change from year to year.
He found a boy asleep at seven and gave him tea instead of a punishment.
One decision tells you what kind of person he is.
He speaks very little and notices everything that happens.
The two things together explain him.

A list of everyone who works at the school
seeds.title: Describing a person for a project
seeds.sub: Who they are, in facts and one story

seeds.goal: You can write about plans: what is decided, what is possible, what depends on results, and what you are doing now to prepare.
seeds.why: Plans are where will, going to and the first conditional finally do different jobs — and where most learners use one form for all three.
seeds.ex: Aizhan wrote her plans for a scholarship form and separated the decided from the possible. The panel called it 'realistic'.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what part of the plan depends on the exam results?
seeds.task: Write about your plans for next year (90–120 words): what is already decided, what is still possible, what depends on results, what you are doing now, and one thing you are worried about.
model: Next year I am going to study at a university in Almaty — that part is decided.
I am applying to three programmes, all of them in biology, and the applications go in before 20 June.
If my chemistry result is above 80, I will apply for the state grant; if it is not, my family will pay for the first year and I will work at weekends.
I may also apply to one programme in Astana, but only if my sister moves there in August.
Say what you are doing now
At the moment I am revising chemistry every evening and doing one practice test on Sundays.
What worries me is not the exam but the two weeks between the results and the deadline, when everything happens at once.
Next month I will know the timetable, and then I can plan properly.
phr: Next year I am going to …
I may also … , but only if …
Возможно, я также …, но только если …
Тогда я смогу спланировать всё как следует.
sent: Next year I am going to study in Almaty.
I am applying to three programmes in biology.
The applications go in before the twentieth of June.
If my result is above eighty, I will apply for the grant.
My family will pay for the first year.
I may also apply to one programme in Astana.
At the moment I am revising chemistry every evening.
I do one practice test on Sundays.
What worries me is the two weeks in between.
Next month I will know the timetable.

The decided part of the plan is simple.
Above eighty means the grant; below it means work at weekends.
One number decides how next year looks.
Chemistry every evening and a practice test on Sundays.
What I am doing about it right now.
ideas: A dream about living abroad one day
seeds.title: Plans for next year
seeds.sub: What you will do, and what depends on what

seeds.goal: You can report a small survey: say what you asked, how many people answered, give two or three findings with numbers and end with one suggestion.
seeds.why: This is the first genre where your opinion has to wait until the last paragraph — and that discipline is what B1 and B2 reports are built on.
seeds.ex: Yerlan reported a survey about the school canteen in a hundred words. The canteen changed its opening time.
seeds.read: Read the report and find one thing: what did most students name as the main problem?
seeds.task: Write a short report on a survey in your class (90–120 words): the aim, how many people answered, three findings with numbers, one thing that surprised you and one suggestion.
model: Say what the survey was about
This report presents the results of a survey about the school canteen.
Twenty-six students of class 9B answered five questions on paper during the long break on 12 March.
First, twenty-one students said that the main problem is the queue, not the food.
Second, on average students wait nine minutes, which leaves eleven minutes to eat.
Third, only four students said the prices were too high.
What surprised us was that nobody complained about the taste of the food, although everybody complains about it in the corridor.
We suggest opening the second window at twelve o'clock, because the queue disappears completely when both windows work.
phr: This report presents the results of …
sent: This report presents the results of a survey.
Twenty-one students said the queue is the main problem.
On average students wait nine minutes.
That leaves eleven minutes to eat.
Only four students said the prices were too high.
Nobody complained about the taste of the food.
Everybody complains about it in the corridor.
We suggest opening the second window at twelve.
The queue disappears when both windows work.
topics: Twenty-six students, five questions, one long break in March.
The method comes before any number.
Twenty-one named the queue; four named the prices.
The findings point in one direction.
Nobody wrote about the taste, although everybody talks about it.
One result contradicted what we expected.
ideas: What we asked and how many answered
My personal opinion about the food
A complaint about one member of staff
seeds.title: A short class report
seeds.sub: What we asked, what we found

seeds.goal: You can write a short article: open with something that stops the reader, explain what the hobby is, give one surprising detail, say what it costs and invite the reader in.
seeds.why: An article is written for people who did not choose to read it. That changes the first sentence completely.
seeds.ex: Sanzhar wrote about bouldering for the school magazine. Six people came to the climbing wall the next Saturday.
seeds.read: Read the article and find one thing: what does the writer say is the real difficulty of this hobby?
seeds.task: Write an article about your hobby (90–120 words): open with a fact or a question, explain what it is, give one surprising detail, say what it costs and what it needs, and invite the reader to try it.
model: The first time I climbed a four-metre wall, I spent eleven minutes on it and moved about a metre.
Bouldering is climbing without a rope, on walls low enough to jump down from, over a thick mat.
The surprising part is that it is not about strength: the strongest boy in our class gave up after three weeks, and a girl who cannot do a single pull-up is now the best in the group.
The real difficulty is reading the wall before you touch it and moving your feet, not your hands.
A session in Almaty costs 2,500 tenge, shoes are 1,000 to hire, and you need nothing else.
Nobody there cares how badly you climb; half of the room is watching a route and arguing about it.
If you have two free hours on a Saturday, come once. You will fail the easiest route and want to come back.
phr: If you have two free hours, come once.
Если есть два свободных часа, приходи разок.
Екі сағат бос болса, бір келіп көр.
You will want to come back.
sent: The first time I climbed I moved about a metre.
Bouldering is climbing without a rope.
The walls are low enough to jump down from.
It is not about strength at all.
The strongest boy in our class gave up after three weeks.
A girl who cannot do a pull-up is now the best.
The real difficulty is reading the wall before you touch it.
A session costs two thousand five hundred tenge.
Nobody cares how badly you climb.
You will fail the easiest route and come back.
topics: Eleven minutes on the wall and about a metre of progress.
The article starts with my worst attempt.
The strongest boy gave up; a girl who cannot do a pull-up is the best.
The surprising part is what does not matter.
2,500 for a session, 1,000 for shoes, nothing else.
The cost is small enough to state exactly.
ideas: An opening that stops the reader
The full history of the sport
A list of my own results
seeds.title: An article about a hobby
seeds.sub: Make a stranger interested in ten lines

seeds.goal: You can write to an office: say who you are, why you are writing, ask one or two exact questions and say what you will do next.
seeds.why: Offices answer emails that identify the writer and ask a checkable question. Everything else waits in a folder.
seeds.ex: Nurai wrote to a language school with her name, group and two numbered questions. The answer came the same day.
seeds.read: Read the email and find one thing: what two questions does the writer ask?
seeds.task: Write an email to a school or course office (80–110 words): who you are, why you are writing, two exact questions, one practical detail about yourself, and a polite close.
model: My name is Nurai Amanova. I am in the Tuesday and Thursday group with Ms Kim, student number 3418.
I am writing about the level test at the end of the course.
First, is the test on 22 or 24 May? The two dates appear on different pages of your website.
Second, if a student misses the test because of illness, is there a second date, or do they take it with the next group?
I ask because I have a school examination on 22 May that I cannot move.
Thank you in advance. Yours faithfully, Nurai Amanova.
phr: First, is the test on … or …?
Second, if a student … , is there …?
The two dates appear on different pages.
Две даты указаны на разных страницах.
sent: My name is Nurai and my student number is 3418.
I am in the Tuesday and Thursday group.
I am writing about the level test.
Is the test on the twenty-second or the twenty-fourth?
The two dates appear on different pages of your website.
If a student misses the test, is there a second date?
I have a school examination on 22 May.
I have already asked my teacher about it.
Thank you in advance for your answer.
topics: Nurai Amanova, Tuesday and Thursday group, student number 3418.
The email starts by making me findable.
The twenty-second on one page, the twenty-fourth on another.
The first question comes from your own website.
I have a school examination on 22 May that cannot be moved.
The reason I need the answer this week.
ideas: Who I am, with a number
A description of my whole term
An opinion about the website design
seeds.title: An email to a school office
seeds.sub: Business, in six lines

seeds.goal: You can write up a trip: the route and the cost, what you did, one thing that went wrong, one practical tip and whether you would repeat it.
seeds.why: The useful part of any trip text is the practical detail: times, prices and the mistake you made.
seeds.ex: Timur wrote up a day trip to the mountains with the bus number and the price. Four classmates used the text as a plan.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what practical tip does the writer give?
seeds.task: Write up a day trip (90–120 words): where you went and how, what it cost, what you did, one thing that went wrong, one practical tip and whether it was worth it.
model: Say where you went and how
Last Sunday four of us went to Big Almaty Lake by bus number 28 and then on foot.
The whole day cost about 3,000 tenge each, including the bus, the entrance to the park and food we bought in the morning.
The bus took fifty minutes and the walk up took nearly three hours, which is more than the internet promised.
We ate at the top, took the same twenty photographs as everybody else and sat in the sun for an hour.
Our mistake was the water: we took one bottle each and finished it before we reached the lake.
Take two litres per person and start before eight, because after eleven the last part of the road has no shade at all.
Say whether it was worth it
Would I go again? Yes, but in September, and with a bus ticket back that I had already bought.
phr: Last Sunday four of us went to …
В прошлое воскресенье мы вчетвером поехали в …
The whole day cost about … each.
Весь день обошёлся примерно в … с человека.
The walk up took nearly … hours.
Would I go again? Yes, but …
Тағы барар ма едім? Иә, бірақ …
sent: Last Sunday four of us went to the lake.
We took bus number twenty-eight and then walked.
The whole day cost about three thousand tenge each.
The walk up took nearly three hours.
We finished our water before we reached the lake.
Take two litres of water per person.
After eleven the road has no shade at all.
I would go again in September.
The way down was much faster than the way up.
topics: Bus 28, fifty minutes, then nearly three hours on foot.
The route is longer than the internet says.
One bottle each, finished before we reached the lake.
Our mistake was simple and avoidable.
Two litres per person, and start before eight because of the shade.
The advice that actually matters.
ideas: A list of every photograph we took
seeds.title: A day trip write-up
seeds.sub: Where you went and whether it was worth it

seeds.goal: You can thank somebody properly: say what for, name one specific thing you remember, say what it gave you and offer something back.
seeds.why: Generic thanks are forgotten in a minute. One exact detail turns a message into something people keep.
seeds.ex: Dana thanked a host family and named one Tuesday evening. They wrote back the same day and invited her again.
seeds.read: Read the message and find one thing: which evening does the writer mention?
seeds.task: Write a thank-you message after staying with somebody (80–110 words): thank them, name one specific memory, say what you learned or gained, mention a small gift and invite them back.
model: Say thank you and what for
Thank you for the two weeks in your house — I arrived as a guest and left feeling like part of the family.
I keep thinking about the Tuesday evening when the electricity went off and we spent three hours playing cards by candlelight.
My English changed more in those two weeks than in a year of lessons, mostly because you never switched to Russian when I got stuck.
I left a box of Kazakh sweets in the kitchen cupboard, on the left, where Anna keeps the tea.
If you ever come to Almaty, my family has a spare room and my mother has been waiting for a reason to cook for guests.
Thank you again for everything. Dana.
phr: Thank you for the two weeks in …
I arrived as a guest and left …
I keep thinking about the … when …
My English changed more in … than in …
Мой английский изменился за … больше, чем за …
I left … in the kitchen cupboard.
I hope to see you again.
sent: Thank you for the two weeks in your house.
I arrived as a guest and left as family.
The electricity went off on Tuesday evening.
We played cards for three hours by candlelight.
My English changed more in two weeks than in a year.
You never switched to Russian when I got stuck.
I left a box of sweets in the kitchen cupboard.
My family has a spare room in Almaty.
My mother has been waiting for a reason to cook.
Thank you again for everything you did.
topics: The Tuesday when the electricity went off and we played cards for three hours.
One evening stands for the whole two weeks.
You never switched to Russian when I got stuck.
The reason my English moved so fast.
A box of sweets in the kitchen cupboard, on the left.
The small thing I left behind.
ideas: What I am thanking them for

A list of everything we ate
seeds.title: A thank-you message after a visit
seeds.sub: Thanks with one real detail

seeds.goal: You can describe a problem and its solution: the situation, what you tried first, why it failed, what worked and what you would do differently.
seeds.why: This is the shape of every interview answer and every project report you will ever write: problem, attempt, result.
seeds.ex: Bekzat wrote about a broken group project. His teacher used it as the model answer for the whole class.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: why did the first attempt fail?
seeds.task: Write about a problem you solved (90–120 words): the situation, what you tried first, why it did not work, what worked in the end, and what you would do differently next time.
model: Two weeks before our history presentation, three of the five people in the group had done nothing at all.
First I sent a long message in the chat with a list of tasks and three exclamation marks.
Nothing happened, because a message to five people is a message to nobody: everybody assumed somebody else would start.
Then I wrote to each person separately, with one task and one date, and asked for a yes or a no.
Two answered in ten minutes and started that evening. The third said honestly that he could not do it, and we gave his part to somebody else.
We finished the presentation two days before the deadline, which had never happened to me before.
Next time I will not write a group message at all: one person, one task, one date.
phr: Two weeks before … , three of five people …
За две недели до … трое из пяти …
… дейін екі апта қалғанда бестің үшеуі …
Then I wrote to each person separately.
В следующий раз я не буду …
One person, one task, one date.
Один человек, одна задача, один срок.
Бір адам, бір тапсырма, бір мерзім.

First I sent a long message in the chat.
Everybody assumed somebody else would start.
Then I wrote to each person separately.
I gave each of them one task and one date.
Two of them answered in ten minutes.
The third said honestly that he could not do it.
We finished two days before the deadline.
Next time I will write to people one by one.
topics: Two weeks left and three of the five had done nothing.
The situation, in one sentence.
A message to five people is a message to nobody.
Why the first attempt failed.
One person, one task, one date, and a yes or no.
What actually worked.
ideas: A description of the presentation topic
seeds.title: A problem and how you solved it
seeds.sub: The situation, the attempts, the solution

seeds.goal: You can write about a book or a film: what it is about without spoiling it, what worked for you, what did not, and who you would give it to.
seeds.why: At this level a review stops being 'I liked it' and starts being a judgement with a reason and a reader in mind.
seeds.ex: Aisha wrote about a novel in a hundred words and named exactly who should not read it. That line got quoted back to her.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: who does the writer say should not read this book?
seeds.task: Write about a book or film you finished recently (90–120 words): the title and type, what it is about without the ending, one thing that worked, one that did not, and who should read or watch it.
model: Name the work and its type
I have just finished 'Wonder' by R. J. Palacio, a novel for teenagers about a boy with a facial difference.
Say what it is about, no ending
August is ten and goes to school for the first time, after years of being taught at home.
Say something about how it is written
The best decision in the book is that the story is told by six different people, including the sister who is tired of being invisible.
Say what worked, with a detail
The chapters written by the sister are the strongest: she loves her brother and she is angry, and the book lets both be true.
The teacher's chapters are weaker, because he is right about everything and no real teacher is.
I would give it to anybody between eleven and fifteen, and also to adults who think children's books are simple.
It took me three evenings, and I have already lent it to two people.

Я только что закончил … — роман о …
… is … and goes to school for the first time.
… … лет, и он впервые идёт в школу.
The best decision in the book is that …
Лучшее решение в книге — то, что …
… and the book lets both be true.
… и книга позволяет обоим быть правдой.
… кітап екеуін де шындық деп қабылдайды.
I would give it to anybody between … and …
Я дал бы её любому от … до …
Мен оны … мен … аралығындағы кез келгенге берер едім.
I have already lent it to two people.
Я уже дал её почитать двоим.

August is ten and goes to school for the first time.
The story is told by six different people.
The sister is tired of being invisible.
The chapters written by the sister are the strongest.
She loves her brother and she is angry.
The teacher's chapters are weaker than the others.
No real teacher is right about everything.
It took me three evenings to read it.
I have already lent it to two people.

seeds.goal: You can write about changing a habit: the situation before, what you changed, how hard the first weeks were, the result and whether it lasted.
seeds.why: Every text about self-improvement is the same until it includes the part that failed. That is the paragraph readers believe.
seeds.ex: Yerkin wrote about giving up energy drinks and included the week he went back to them. The honesty is why people finished it.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what happened in the third week?
seeds.task: Write about a habit you changed (90–120 words): what it was like before, what exactly you changed, the hardest part, what happened when you failed, and whether the change lasted.
model: Last year I was drinking two cans of energy drink a day, usually at eleven in the morning and at four in the afternoon.
I stopped after a week when I could not sleep before two in the morning and fell asleep in a biology lesson.
I did not give up caffeine completely — that failed twice before. I replaced the morning can with tea and kept the afternoon one for two weeks.
The hardest part was not the tiredness but the habit of walking to the shop at the same time every day.
Say what happened when it went wrong
In the third week I had two exams and drank three cans in one day, which was more than before.
Say what you did about it
Instead of giving up on the whole thing, I started again on the Monday, and that decision is the only reason it worked.
That was eight months ago. I drink one can a month now, usually when somebody buys me one.

В прошлом году я пил … в день.
I stopped after a week when …
I did not give up … completely.
The hardest part was not … but …

Вместо того чтобы бросить, я начал заново в понедельник.

I could not sleep before two in the morning.
I fell asleep in a biology lesson.
I did not give up caffeine completely.
I replaced the morning can with tea.
The hardest part was the habit of walking to the shop.
In the third week I drank three cans in one day.
I started again on the Monday.
That decision is the only reason it worked.
I drink one can a month now.

The habit had a shape before it had a problem.
Not the tiredness, but walking to the shop at the same time every day.
The hardest part was not what I expected.

seeds.title: A habit you changed
seeds.sub: What you did, and whether it lasted

seeds.goal: You can write a short news note: put the result in the first sentence, add when and who, include one quotation and say what happens next.
seeds.why: News writing forces the most useful habit in any text: the most important fact goes first, not last.
seeds.ex: Alina's note about a school competition opened with the result. The class page got its highest number of readers that week.
seeds.read: Read the note and find one thing: what is the news in the first sentence?
seeds.task: Write a news note for a class page (80–110 words): the news in the first sentence, when and where, who took part, one detail, one short quotation and what happens next.
model: Our class won the school quiz for the first time in six years.
The final took place in the assembly hall on Friday, 14 March, in front of about two hundred students.
Six classes reached the final, and our team of four was the youngest by two years.
The last question was about the boiling point of water at altitude, and we were the only team that answered it.
"We guessed," said Aidos afterwards, "but we guessed together."
The team thanks Ms Iskakova, who spent four lunch breaks asking us questions we could not answer.
The city competition is on 25 April, and the team is looking for a fifth member — anybody who knows geography should talk to Aidos.

Наш класс выиграл … впервые за … лет.
Our team was the youngest by two years.
Наша команда была младше на два года.
Біздің команда екі жасқа кіші болды.

The final took place in the assembly hall.
About two hundred students watched the final.
Six classes reached the final this year.
Our team was the youngest by two years.
The last question was about the boiling point of water.
We were the only team that answered it.
Ms Iskakova spent four lunch breaks with us.

The team is looking for a fifth member.

seeds.sub: The news first, the details after

seeds.goal: You can explain your country or city to a foreign friend: what surprises visitors, what is normal for you, one thing that is hard to explain and what they should not miss.
seeds.why: Explaining your own place is the most common real task abroad — and the hardest to improvise, because everything obvious to you is new to them.
seeds.ex: Miras answered a Polish friend's question about Kazakhstan in a hundred words. His friend printed it before her trip.
seeds.read: Read the email and find one thing: what does the writer say surprises visitors most?
seeds.task: Write an email to a friend abroad about your country or city (90–120 words): what surprises visitors, one thing that is normal for you, one thing that is hard to explain, what they should try and one practical warning.
model: You asked what surprises visitors most here. Everybody says the same thing: the distances.
From my city to the next big one is a thirteen-hour train journey, and on the map it looks like nothing.
Say what is normal for you
What is completely normal for us is tea: it is not a drink, it is what happens when somebody arrives, at any hour, and refusing it is genuinely strange.
Say what is hard to explain
The hard thing to explain is that most people here switch between two languages inside one sentence and do not notice it.
When you come, try beshbarmak once and go to a bazaar in the morning rather than the afternoon — after two o'clock the good things are gone.
One warning: in July the city is thirty-five degrees at nine in the morning, so plan everything before eleven.
phr: You asked what surprises visitors most.
Ты спрашивала, что больше всего удивляет гостей.
Все говорят одно и то же: …
What is completely normal for us is …
The hard thing to explain is that …
sent: You asked what surprises visitors most here.
Everybody says the same thing about the distances.
From my city to the next one is thirteen hours by train.
On the map it looks like nothing.
Tea is what happens when somebody arrives.
Refusing it is genuinely strange here.
Most people switch between two languages in one sentence.
Go to the bazaar in the morning, not the afternoon.
In July it is thirty-five degrees at nine in the morning.
topics: Thirteen hours by train to the next big city, and on the map it looks small.

tr.why: Although turns two facts into one sentence with a clear relationship.

ans: I have been doing this course since September.

ans: Could you tell me the result, please?
tr.why: Could you…? turns an order into a request, even between classmates.

tr.src: Maybe it rains tomorrow. Then we stay at home.
ans: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
tr.why: The if-clause uses the present, the main clause uses will.

tr.src: This café is cheap. That café is not cheap.
ans: This café is cheaper than that one.
tr.why: A comparison needs the comparative form plus than.

tr.src: Somebody stole my bike last week.
ans: My bike was stolen last week.
tr.why: When the person is unknown, English moves the object to the front.

tr.why: Going to is for decisions you have already made.

rubric.task: Is every part of the task covered, and does the text do what the genre is for?
rubric.organisation: Two or three paragraphs, one idea each, with linking words between the sentences.
rubric.vocabulary: Topic words and precise adjectives instead of good, bad and very.
rubric.grammar: Past and perfect forms, articles, prepositions, comparatives and simple relative clauses.
